evidence.claims: Backed: headline ranges (0.05-9.4 N, 1.3-1000x, ~40%% agreement, ~3x from tip size) all reproduce from results.txt and my script; coefficient sources match the cited PDF; 'not a safety case' and AI-assistance disclosure present. Not backed: Limitations line 38 says 'the budget (chi ~ 0.3 to 0.6) is inside the range the source studies' - the budget cells span chi = 0.245..0.949, and the cited source validates the corrections by FEA only for 0 < chi < 0.4 (Dal Fabbro et al. sec. 4.1.3) and Hertz/LIC up to delta/R = 1, while 21 of 36 budget cells have chi > 0.4 and 6 have delta/R > 1. The trial forces 12.6/20.2/53.3 N and 'kinematic lips have stiffness 75,000 N/m' (README:14) come from osrobot-mjpress, which reuses the osrobot-mjface model that carries a 2026-11-13 correction (solref units: face is 22,500 N/m, worst peak at b=1000 ~204 N); this README does not mention it. The headline range '0.05 to 9.4 N' mixes the Dimitriadis minimum with the Garcia maximum without saying so (minor).
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it and one did (osrobot-mjsoft takes its next step). But as research it is one closed-form evaluation of two published AFM bottom-effect polynomials on a 36-cell grid; no FE check, no large-indentation correction, no nonlinear material, not part of any programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md, so it sits well below the PhD/programme bar in research/CLAUDE.md. Nearest prior work: Dimitriadis et al. 2002 and Garcia & Garcia 2018 (the corrections), Dal Fabbro et al. 2024 (FEA validation, used), Long et al. 2011 (neo-Hookean thin-layer indentation at large strain, not cited), ISO/TS 15066 Annex A and the Mainz pain-onset study behind it (Melia et al. 2015), and robot-assisted feeding work (e.g. Gallenberger et al. 2019; Bhattacharjee et al. 2020) for practical bite-transfer force levels, none compared. The qualitative conclusion (newton-scale cap) is sound and robust; the method is not new.
evidence.domain: Against contact-mechanics practice: the polynomials are used for a sphere at delta/R up to 1.5 without the large-indentation (Kontomaris/Muller) or Sneddon correction that the cited source itself says is needed as delta/R approaches 1; at chi up to 0.95, more than twice the FEA-validated 0.4; with linear elasticity at 30 %% compressive strain where hyperelastic stiffening (Long et al. 2011) matters; and with a flat bonded rigid substrate for a lip that has teeth and an air cavity behind it. The 30 %% depth limit is the author's choice and is not an injury or pain criterion; an ISO/TS 15066 practitioner would ask for pressure/pain thresholds instead. Limits are stated, but the range claim is wrong, so the method is not one a reviewer would sign off as-is.

No large-indentation correction (Kontomaris/Muller) or Sneddon sphere model although delta/R reaches 1.5 at the budget; the cited paper says Hertz needs delta << R and pairs the bottom-effect correction with an LIC for large indentation. Linear elasticity at 30 % strain, no hyperelastic check (Long et al. 2011).

Trial forces (53.3/20.2/12.6 N) and the 75,000 N/m lip stiffness come from osrobot-mjpress, built on the osrobot-mjface model whose 2026-11-13 correction (MuJoCo solref read per kg: face 22,500 N/m, worst b=1000 peak ~204 N) changes them; this README does not note it. The conclusion's direction survives (forces exceed the budget by more), the ratios do not.

Tests pin no number: sign flip of a coefficient, a 10x Garcia coefficient and a 3x change in the 30 % depth limit all leave the 6 tests green; no test compares to a published coefficient set or to results.txt.
Headline range '0.05 to 9.4 N' takes the minimum from Dimitriadis and the maximum from Garcia without saying so (Dimitriadis max is 8.67 N).

Single closed-form evaluation outside any research programme; no FE cross-check, prior work on large-strain thin-layer indentation and on feeding-robot contact forces not compared; below the research/CLAUDE.md PhD/programme bar.

verdict: A genuine but small research note, not a stub: two published bottom-effect polynomials for a sphere on a bonded incompressible layer, evaluated on a 36-cell grid to give a 'force budget' at 30 % depth. Every number reproduces, the coefficients match the cited PDF and an independent derivation from Dimitriadis 2002, and the qualitative message (a newton-scale force cap, not 65 N) is robust. It misses the bar on verification (3 of 4 seeded mutants survive; no test pins a number) and claims: the README states the budget sits inside the source's validated range when most cells (chi up to 0.95, delta/R up to 1.5) are beyond it, and the upstream trial forces it compares against predate the osrobot-mjface solref correction. A contact-mechanics reviewer would also ask for a large-indentation correction and a hyperelastic or FE check. Median 2; finished (completeness 3) but not expert-grade.
